# 1. Executive Summary

This report identifies unusual patterns in retail transactions using statistical analysis.

# 2. Load Data

```{r setup, include=FALSE} id="k7p4x2"
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)

retail_clean <- readRDS("../data/processed/retail_cleaned.rds")
```

# 3. Revenue Summary

```{r} id="m8q2w5"
revenue_summary <- retail_clean %>%
  summarise(
    Total_Revenue = sum(Revenue, na.rm = TRUE),
    Average_Revenue = mean(Revenue, na.rm = TRUE),
    Revenue_SD = sd(Revenue, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

kable(revenue_summary, digits = 2)
```

# 4. Identify Unusual Revenue Transactions

The analysis uses the interquartile range (IQR) method to flag unusually high or low transaction revenue values.

```{r} id="n3v6b9"
q1 <- quantile(retail_clean$Revenue, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE)
q3 <- quantile(retail_clean$Revenue, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE)
iqr_value <- IQR(retail_clean$Revenue, na.rm = TRUE)

lower_limit <- q1 - 1.5 * iqr_value
upper_limit <- q3 + 1.5 * iqr_value

anomalies <- retail_clean %>%
  filter(Revenue < lower_limit | Revenue > upper_limit)

anomaly_summary <- data.frame(
  Lower_Limit = lower_limit,
  Upper_Limit = upper_limit,
  Anomaly_Count = nrow(anomalies),
  Anomaly_Percentage = round(nrow(anomalies) / nrow(retail_clean) * 100, 2)
)

kable(anomaly_summary, digits = 2)
```

# 5. Anomaly Visualization

```{r} id="p5r8s1"
ggplot(retail_clean, aes(x = Revenue)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 50, fill = "steelblue", color = "white") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = upper_limit, color = "red", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = lower_limit, color = "darkorange", linewidth = 1) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = quantile(retail_clean$Revenue, c(0.01, 0.99), na.rm = TRUE)) +
  labs(
    title = "Revenue Distribution and Anomaly Limits",
    x = "Transaction Revenue",
    y = "Frequency"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

# 6. Sample Anomalies

```{r} id="t2u6w9"
anomalies %>%
  select(Invoice, StockCode, Description, Quantity, Price, Revenue, Country) %>%
  arrange(desc(abs(Revenue))) %>%
  head(20) %>%
  kable()
```

# 7. Business Insights

- Unusually high or low transaction values may require further investigation.
- High-value transactions can be reviewed for unusual purchasing patterns.
- Negative revenue transactions may relate to returns or cancellations.
- Statistical anomalies do not automatically indicate fraud or errors.

# 8. Recommendations

1. Review unusually high-value transactions.
2. Investigate unusual negative revenue records.
3. Monitor transaction patterns regularly.
4. Validate suspicious records before making business decisions.

# 9. Conclusion

The IQR method provides a simple way to identify unusual transaction revenue values. These results can help businesses investigate exceptional transactions.

**Data Limitation:** Anomalies are statistical flags based on transaction revenue, not confirmed fraud or data errors. The dataset covers December 2009 to December 2011.
